Rajesh on 6 February, 2025

Author: Rajasekhar Mantha
Bench: Rajasekhar Mantha

06.02.2025
 ct.13
Sl. no.28
 p.k. I.A. No. Cran 3 of 2024

In
 C.R.A. 456 of 2016

In the matter of: An application for suspension of sentence in
 connection with appeal under Section 389(1) of the Code of
 Criminal Procedure, 1973.

And
 In re.: Ranbir Ekka @ Rajesh ... Appellant.
 Ms. Ashima Mandla,
 Ms. Mandakini Singh,
 Ms. Ritu Das,
 Mr. Vipul Pathak
 . ... for the Appellant.
 Re: Cran 3 of 2024
 1.

An application for suspension of sentence is based on the (a)
 delay in lodging of the complaint with the police, (b)
 inconsistency in the disclosure of the identification of the  appellant by the prosecutrix, (c) contradiction of the 164  statement, the deposition in Court of the prosecutrix and (d)
 the absence of the independent witness.
 2. On the argument (a) it is stated that while the incident  occurred on 07.02.2014, the prosecutrix only informed her  maternal grandmother, about that same, upon being probed  on 10.02.2014.
She was taken by the parents to a child  specialist when the incident complained of was detected.

The An Application For Suspension Of ... vs In Re.: Ranbir Ekka @ Rajesh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71575521/
1  complaint was filed two days after the incident when the FIR  was registered

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: . The delay in lodging of complaint with the  police, according to the learned counsel for the appellant, is  fatal to the prosecution and conviction of the appellant.

3. This Court is of the view that in cases of this nature under  the POCSO Act when the victim is seven years old a  2  discomfort expressed by the child to her parents is not ipso  facto lead to a suspicion of commission of an offence.
The  delay of lodging an FIR, even otherwise, is not fatal to a  prosecution case, as has been held by the Supreme Court in  several cases.
4. On the argument (b) the disclosure by the prosecutrix, vis a  vis identification of the appellant by the prosecution it is

submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the  PW 1(Father of the prosecutirx) and the I O have deposed that  the accused has been identified in the police station where as  PW 4, Aunt of the prosecutrix stated that the appellant was  identified in the school magazine.
The aforesaid is not such a  serious infirmity if at all to discard evidence of the witness of  the prosecution.

5. Insofar as point no. (c) i.e. alleged contradiction between the  statements under 164 of the Cr. P. C. and the evidence of the  prosecutrix in Court, it is pointed out in the statement under  Section 164 the victim stated that the appellant committed An Application For Suspension Of ... vs In Re.: Ranbir Ekka @ Rajesh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71575521/
2  rape on the victim at the school terrace and later brought her  down and left her near the class room.

In the trial, however,
 the appellant has stated that he left her in the terrace after  committing offence and she came down on her own where the  appellant took her near the class room.
This Court does not  see any serious contradiction in the evidence of the  prosecutrix in this regard.
6. The alleged threat by the appellant to the victim indicated in  the statement under Section 164 was not stated in course of  trial.
3 7. Admittedly, there was no eye witness to the incident.
The  victim did not complain to her school mates or the teaching  and non teaching staff until she reached home and informed  her parents for the first time about her discomfort.

It is  normal for a seven years old child to repose an incident of  this nature in her mother and father rather than disclose the  same with her class mates or the teachers in the school.
8.

This Court is of the view that the discrepancies indicated by  the learned counsel for the appellant is far too minor to  dislodge the evidence of the other witnesses and the other  evidence of the victim in course of trial.
9. It is lastly argued that there are no independent witnesses  who were examined in course of trial namely other students  of the school and the other teaching and non teaching staff.

It  is now well settled that in some cases of charges under the An Application For Suspension Of ... vs In Re.: Ranbir Ekka @ Rajesh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71575521/
3 POCSO Act and 376 of IPC the testimony of the victim alone  is sufficient.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case the family of the victim and  the medical evidence corroborates the evidence of the  prosecutrix.
10. Having regard to the aforesaid, this Court is not inclined  to suspend the sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, CRAN  3 of 2024 is dismissed.

Since it appears from the records that the preparation of  paper of books have not yet been prepared, the Registry shall  ensure preparation of paper books as expeditiously as  possible and notify the counsel for the appellant and the
State .
4 12. List this appeal on 18.03.2024.
13. All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly  downloaded from the official website of this Court.

. 
(Rajasekhar Mantha, J.) (Ajay Kumar Gupta, J.)
